name: application-radar-chart
title: Radar Chart
description: Multi-axis polygon comparison for skill or feature profiles, with the filled shape, grid rings, and axis spokes all computed from real per-axis values via trigonometry.
useWhen: Comparing an entity across several qualitative dimensions at once (e.g. Speed/Design/Reliability/Support/Price).
The overall "shape" of a profile matters more than reading exact values off an axis.
You have 3–8 axes — few enough that a polygon stays legible.
avoidWhen: You need to compare more than a couple of series on the same chart — overlapping polygons get hard to read fast.
Precise value comparison matters more than overall shape — a bar chart or bullet-chart communicates exact values better.
You have only 1–2 axes — a radar chart needs at least 3 to read as a polygon.
responsiveBehavior: The chart is a fixed-size SVG (default 220px) centered in a card; scale the `size` prop for the surrounding layout rather than relying on CSS scaling.
accessibility: The SVG carries role='img' with an aria-label listing every axis name and value, since the polygon shape alone isn't announced by screen readers.
Every axis value is also shown as visible text in the legend grid below the chart.
Grid rings and axis spokes are low-contrast supporting lines, not required for interpreting the data — the filled polygon and legend carry the meaning.

variants.title: Radar chart
variants.description: Five-axis vendor comparison (Speed/Design/Reliability/Support/Price) as a filled polygon over grid rings, on a light surface.
accessibility: Polygon fill and stroke color is supplementary; the legend grid's numeric values carry the precise data.

variants.title: Radar chart (Dark)
variants.description: The same five-axis vendor comparison, adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Grid, polygon, and text colors must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark backgrounds.
